title: The White Lily Pharmacy
teaser: The pharmacy closed at eight, but the light in the back room stayed on longer than usual. Pharmacist Arnaud knew what went into every powder and would never have got a dose wrong, yet her cup held something she never drank. The poison was mixed in behind locked doors, which means someone stayed after closing.

habits.label: Tar soap
clues: The towel in the back room reeks of tar, and the pharmacy only keeps toilet soap. The culprit's hands smell of tar soap.
The handle of the lab door smells of tar soap. The culprit's hands smell of tar soap.

habits.label: Cinnamon coffee
clues: There are specks of cinnamon on a saucer in the back room, and Arnaud couldn't stand cinnamon. The culprit drinks coffee with cinnamon.
A tin on the back-room shelf holds freshly ground cinnamon that wasn't there yesterday. The culprit drinks coffee with cinnamon.

habits.label: Dragonfly brooch
habits.habit: A dragonfly brooch on the lapel
clues: A green glass piece from the wing of a dragonfly brooch was found under the table in the back room. The culprit wears a dragonfly brooch.
The last customer remembers a dragonfly brooch on someone's lapel at the counter at five to eight. The culprit wears a dragonfly brooch.

habits.label: Scar on the thumb
clues: The glass of a measuring beaker has a thumbprint crossed by the line of a scar. The culprit has a scar on their thumb.
The sealing wax on a vial in the lab bears the print of a thumb with a scar across it. The culprit has a scar on their thumb.

habits.label: Mole on the cheek
habits.habit: A large mole on the cheek
clues: From the back yard the caretaker saw a face with a dark mole on the cheek in the back-room window. The culprit has a mole on their cheek.
Arnaud's notebook has a note: "After closing again, the same mole on the cheek." The culprit has a mole on their cheek.

habits.label: Ink on the fingers
clues: The edge of a prescription form in the back room has a smudged violet fingerprint. The culprit has ink on their fingers.
The handle of the cup has a violet stain, and Arnaud only ever wrote in black ink. The culprit's fingers are stained with violet ink.

habits.label: Locket
habits.habit: A locket with a photograph around the neck
clues: A bit of fine chain with the loop from a locket lies on the back-room floor. The culprit wears a locket.
Arnaud's fingers clutch a tiny photograph, trimmed into an oval exactly the size of a locket. The culprit wears a locket with a photograph.

habits.label: Knits
clues: A ball of grey wool with a needle stuck through it is behind a cupboard in the back room. The culprit knits.
A steel knitting needle was left on the waiting-room windowsill, and Arnaud never knitted. The culprit knits.

habits.label: Violin
clues: There's white rosin dust on the arm of a chair in the waiting room. The culprit plays the violin.
The neighbour through the wall heard someone tuning a violin in the pharmacy after closing. The culprit plays the violin.

habits.label: Canary
clues: There's a yellow canary feather on Arnaud's sleeve. The culprit keeps a canary.
Birdseed from a paper twist is scattered on the back-room floor. The culprit keeps a canary at home.

habits.label: Sneezes at flowers
clues: The white lilies from the shop window have been carried out to the back yard, though they're only changed on Saturdays. The culprit sneezes at flower pollen.
After eight the watchman heard repeated sneezing from the back room. The culprit sneezes at pollen.

habits.label: Velvet beret
habits.habit: Wears a velvet beret at an angle
clues: Dark velvet pile was left on a coat hook in the waiting room. The culprit wears a velvet beret.
A passer-by saw a silhouette in a beret worn at an angle by the pharmacy's back door. The culprit wears a velvet beret.

habits.label: Shorthand
clues: The back of a prescription in the back room has a line of shorthand squiggles. The culprit knows shorthand.
A shorthand note has come off on the blotter in the owner's office. The culprit takes everything down in shorthand.

habits.label: Draws portraits
clues: The wrapping paper in the back room has a sketch of Arnaud's profile, done by a skilled hand. The culprit draws portraits.
A rolled-paper blending stump, black with graphite, lies on the floor by the counter. The culprit draws portraits in pencil.

habits.label: Bitten nails
clues: A form in the back room has a fingerprint with a nail bitten to the quick. The culprit has bitten nails.
There are bitten-off slivers of fingernail on the back-room windowsill. The culprit has bitten nails.

habits.label: Language of flowers
clues: Yellow carnations were left on the counter, and in the language of flowers they mean contempt. The culprit knows the language of flowers.
Someone pinned a sprig of basil to Arnaud's blouse, which in the language of flowers means hatred. The culprit knows the language of flowers.

medic: Arnaud's cup holds a poison that doesn't taste bitter in tea, and the dose was judged exactly. The culprit knows about poisons.
The vial taken from the cabinet in the medicine store was precisely the one whose contents have no smell. The culprit knows about poisons.
tools: The catch on the back-room window was unscrewed and screwed back with the same screws. The culprit is handy with tools.
The seal on the store cabinet was taken off with tweezers and put back so it can't be told apart. The culprit is handy with tools.
cash: The day's takings have been counted, but two large notes are missing from the drawer. The culprit had access to money.
The last sale has been erased from the pharmacy's receipts book. The culprit had access to money.
safe: The safe in the owner's office was opened without force, and the poisons register is gone. The culprit knows the safe combination.
The safe's dial is set to zero, though the owner always spins it to random numbers. The culprit knows the safe combination.
glasses: A round lens that fell out of its frame lies on the back-room floor. The culprit wears glasses.
A prescription by the till has a dent from the arm of a pair of glasses. The culprit wears glasses.
driver: There's a fresh van track in the back yard, though the gates were locked at closing. The culprit can drive.
In the morning the pharmacy van isn't parked the way it was in the evening, and the engine hasn't cooled. The culprit can drive.
passages: A delivery door, unknown to customers, leads from the back room to the yard, and it isn't locked. The culprit knows the service passages.
Through the cellar of the medicine store you can get out into the next building, and there are fresh footprints in the dust on the steps. The culprit knows the service passages.
keys: The pharmacy was locked after eight, and there's no sign of a break-in. The culprit had keys.
The poisons cabinet was opened with its own key, the spare of which was thought lost long ago. The culprit had keys.
sched: The watchman walks round the yard at nine, and the back-room door was opened at ten past eight. The culprit knows the schedule.
Every evening at exactly eight Arnaud has tea in the back room, and few people know it. The culprit knows the schedule.
quiet: The bell over the shop door didn't ring once. The culprit moves silently.
Arnaud sat with her back to the door and didn't turn round at the footsteps. The culprit moves silently.
cane: There are round dents from a cane in the waiting-room linoleum. The culprit walks with a cane.
At about eight the watchman heard a cane tapping on the flagstones of the back yard. The culprit walks with a cane.
smoker: There's a fresh cigarette end by the back-room door in the yard. The culprit smokes.
The back room, where Arnaud never let anyone smoke, smells of tobacco. The culprit smokes.
perfume: Through the smell of medicines in the back room comes a trail of heavy perfume. The culprit wears heavy perfume.
The handkerchief by the cup is soaked in a thick, sweet perfume. The culprit wears heavy perfume.
french: A prescription in the back room has a note added: "Pour Mathilde, la dernière". The culprit knows French.
The label on a vial has been rewritten in French without a single mistake. The culprit knows French.
late: The watchmaker next door saw a shadow in the pharmacy window after midnight. The culprit doesn't sleep at night.
The watchman says glassware was clinking in the pharmacy late into the night. The culprit is a night owl.
